lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-product-flow-g:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A$ be a self-adjoint
operator on $H$ with domain $D(A)$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), and let $B$ be a
bounded self-adjoint operator on $H$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]],
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]) with
$$B\,e^{isA}=e^{isA}B\qquad(s\in\mathbb R),$$
where $e^{isA}=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{is\lambda}\,dE_A(\lambda)$ is the unitary
group of $A$ in the spectral calculus
([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]],
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Put $A+B$ on its natural domain
$D(A+B):=D(A)\cap D(B)=D(A)$. Then:

(a) $A+B$ is self-adjoint;

(b) $e^{isB}e^{itA}=e^{itA}e^{isB}$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$; the flows of
$A$ and of the bounded $B$ commute;

(c) the family $s\mapsto P(s):=e^{isA}e^{isB}$ is a strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary group
([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]), and its
infinitesimal generator $G$
([[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]) is $G=i(A+B)$: the
quotient $\frac1s\bigl(P(s)x-x\bigr)$ converges as $s\to0$ exactly for
$x\in D(A)$, with limit $i(A+B)x$. Consequently $P(s)=e^{is(A+B)}$ for every
$s\in\mathbb R$.
lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-th:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the cited spectral suppliers. Fix $\hbar>0$ and $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put
$r:=2s+1$, and let
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with inner product linear in the
first argument
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]). Let $SO(3)$ be the
special orthogonal group ([[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]]), let
$U(R)$ for $R\in SO(3)$ be the componentwise spatial rotation action
$$(U(R)f)_{l}(x):=f_{l}(R^{-1}x)\qquad(l=1,\dots,r)$$
of [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]], and let
$\rho_0:SU(2)\to SO(3)$ be the quaternion conjugation cover of
[[ex-su-two-to-so-three-as-a-covering-homomorphism]], using the matrix identification
$$a+bi+cj+dk\longmapsto\begin{pmatrix}a+bi&c+di\\-c+di&a-bi\end{pmatrix}$$
and the imaginary basis $(i,j,k)$ of [[def-cm-quaternion-rotation-map-and-cover]].
For the physical coordinate axes used by the Pauli matrices fix
$$C:=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&-1\\0&-1&0\\-1&0&0\end{pmatrix}\in SO(3),\qquad \rho(W):=C^{-1}\rho_0(W)C.$$
Thus $\rho$ is the same two-sheeted cover transported to the axes
$(Ce_1,Ce_2,Ce_3)=(-e_3,-e_2,-e_1)$; it is not the literal matrix $\rho_0$ in the imaginary basis. It is smooth by
[[def-covering-homomorphism-of-lie-groups]]. Let
$F_{s}:\mathcal S_{2s}\to V_{s}=\mathbb C^{r}$ be the unitary identification
$v_{k}\mapsto e_{s-k}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-symmetric-power-su2-representation]] clause
(d) (for $s=0$, $\mathcal S_{0}=\mathbb C v_{0}$ and $F_{0}v_{0}:=1$),
define $D_{s}:SU(2)\to U(V_{s})$ by
$D_{s}(W):=F_{s}U_{2s}(W)F_{s}^{-1}$ for $s>0$ and
$D_{0}(W):=I_{\mathbb C}$, and let $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the self-adjoint
spin endomorphisms of $V_{s}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (a). By clauses
(b),(d),(f) of the theorem the maps $D_{s}$ are strongly continuous unitary
representations of $SU(2)$.
For $W\in SU(2)$ define the matrix action $M_{s}(W)\in\mathcal B(H_{s})$ and
the lifted operator $U_{s}(W)$ by
$$(M_{s}(W)f)(x):=D_{s}(W)\bigl(f(x)\bigr),\qquad U_{s}(W):=U(\rho(W))\,M_{s}(W)\qquad(f\in H_{s},\ x\in\mathbb R^{3}),$$
where the matrix $D_{s}(W)$ acts on the column vector $f(x)\in\mathbb C^{r}$.
Finally let $R_{i}(t)$, $i=1,2,3$, be the coordinate rotation matrices and
$L_{i}$ the self-adjoint coordinate-rotation generators on $H_{s}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] (so that
$U(R_{i}(t))=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}$), and put
$A_{i}(t):=\cos(t/2)I_{2}-i\sin(t/2)\sigma_{i}\in SU(2)$ with the Pauli
matrices $\sigma_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e). Then:

(a) for every $W\in SU(2)$ the operator $U_{s}(W)$ is unitary, with
$U_{s}(I)=\mathrm{id}$ and $U_{s}(W_{1}W_{2})=U_{s}(W_{1})U_{s}(W_{2})$ for
all $W_{1},W_{2}\in SU(2)$, and $W\mapsto U_{s}(W)$ is strongly continuous
([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]);

(b) $\rho(A_{i}(t))=R_{i}(t)$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$ and every $i$, and
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary
group ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]);

(c) the operators $L_{i}$ and $S_{i}$ strongly commute (their spectral
projection-valued measures commute;
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]],
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]), the sum $J_{i}:=L_{i}+S_{i}$ with
domain $D(J_{i}):=D(L_{i})$ is self-adjoint, and
$$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R);$$
moreover for $W\in SU(2)$ one has the conjugation identities including
domains
$$U_{s}(W)Q_{j}U_{s}(W)^{-1}=\sum_{l=1}^{3}\rho(W)_{lj}Q_{l},\qquad U_{s}(W)P_{k}U_{s}(W)^{-1}=\sum_{l=1}^{3}\rho(W)_{lk}P_{l},$$
where $Q_{j},P_{k}$ are the componentwise position and momentum operators of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a) and
$\rho(W)_{lj}$ are the matrix entries of the transported cover in the standard basis; the sums mean the maximal directional realizations $Q(\rho(W)e_j)$ and $P(\rho(W)e_k)$ of [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]] clause (b), with domains $U_s(W)D(Q_j)$ and $U_s(W)D(P_k)$;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is a mathematical statement about the
finite-dimensional spin representation and the componentwise rotation action;
it asserts no physical interpretation, no measurement, no dynamics and no
value of $\hbar$, $s$ or $W$. The spatial action enters only through
$U(R)=U(\rho(W))$ and the internal action only through $M_{s}(W)$; no action
on a second spatial or internal factor is introduced.
lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-casimi:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
notation of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-laplacian-diagonal-domain]]: $S^2$ with its
polar measure $\sigma$, the Hilbert space $L^{2}(S^2,\sigma)$ with inner
product linear in the first argument
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]), the complete orthonormal
family $(Y_{lm})_{l\ge0,\,-l\le m\le l}$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]]), the blocks
$V_{l}:=\operatorname{span}\{Y_{l,-l},\dots,Y_{ll}\}$, the finite span $H$,
the self-adjoint operators $L_{1},L_{2},L_{3}$ with $L_{3}=L_{z}$ and
$L_{i}Y_{lm}\in V_{l}$ for all $l,m,i$, and the diagonal sphere Laplacian $A$
with $AY_{lm}=l(l+1)Y_{lm}$. Then for every $l\ge0$:

(a) each $L_{i}$ leaves $V_{l}$ invariant, and the restriction
$L_{i}|_{V_{l}}$ is a self-adjoint endomorphism of the finite-dimensional
inner product space $V_{l}$
([[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]]), with
$L_{3}Y_{lm}=\hbar mY_{lm}$ for $-l\le m\le l$;

(b) the triple $\bigl((1/\hbar)L_{1}|_{V_{l}},(1/\hbar)L_{2}|_{V_{l}},(1/\hbar)L_{3}|_{V_{l}}\bigr)$
is unitarily equivalent to the spin-$l$ matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]; in particular
$$\sum_{i=1}^{3}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)F\qquad(F\in V_{l});$$

(c) for every $F$ in the finite span $H$ one has
$\sum_{i=1}^{3}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}AF$.

The statement is a mathematical statement about the operators on
$L^{2}(S^2,\sigma)$; no physical interpretation as angular momentum of a
particle is asserted.

def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angu.physical_scope: The angular momentum readings of the massive spin-s particle model: the orbital generators of the spatial coordinate rotations, the internal spin matrices of the spin assignment P6, and their self-adjoint sum, each read as an assigned sharp observable of the framework with units of action, together with the declaration that the internal factor is not a spatial object. The item fixes terminology and readings of P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6; it asserts no dynamics, no magnetic coupling, no apparatus or detection model, no spin-orbit or relativistic structure and no empirical identification of any laboratory quantity with the operators named.

def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angu:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor
assignment of the identical-particle and spin postulate P6, all read for the
spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with
mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and
$r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Let
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the model's state space with
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$, and let $\mathcal S^{(r)}$ be its
componentwise Schwartz class
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]). Units are
those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the unit of angular
momentum is the unit of action (J$\,$s).

**(b) Orbital angular momentum.** For $i=1,2,3$ let $L_{i}$ be the
self-adjoint operator on $H_{s}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]], the Stone
generator of the coordinate rotation group $t\mapsto U(R_{i}(t))$, so that
$U(R_{i}(t))=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}$ and, on the Schwartz class,
$$L_{i}\psi=\sum_{j,k=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ijk}\,Q_{j}P_{k}\psi$$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] clause (b),
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). The model reads
$(L_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an **assigned sharp observable**, called the
$i$-th **orbital angular momentum** of the model, with outcome law
$\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho}$ in a preparation $\rho$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a),(b),
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). The operators
$L_{i}$ act on the spatial factor only; their reading on the angular degrees
of freedom is the one supplied by the sphere operators
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]], and the finite-blocks identity
$\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)F$ on the harmonic span is the content of a
separate lemma of this page
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-casimir-identity]]).

**(c) Spin angular momentum.** Let $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the internal
operators of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause
(c), the matrix actions $\bigl(S_{i}f\bigr)_{l}=\hbar\sum_{m}(J_{i})_{lm}f_{m}$
of the self-adjoint matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]. The model reads
$(S_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable, the $i$-th **spin
angular momentum**; on the internal factor,
$$[S_{i},S_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ijk}S_{k},\qquad S^{2}:=S_{x}^{2}+S_{y}^{2}+S_{z}^{2}=\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$$
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clauses (a),(b),(c),
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)). The
**ladder** operators $S_{\pm}:=S_{x}\pm iS_{y}$ and the finite projections on
the basis vectors $e_{m}$ are structural objects of the internal factor, not
assigned sharp observables, and $S_{\pm}$ are not self-adjoint. For $s=\tfrac12$
one has $S_{i}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_{i}$ in the Pauli matrices
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e)). The internal
factor is a finite-dimensional bookkeeping factor: it is not a spatial
coordinate, not a rotating body and not a relativistic spinor, and the model
assigns no position or worldline to it.

**(d) Total angular momentum.** For each $i$ let
$$J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}:=L_{i}+S_{i},\qquad D(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}):=D(L_{i}),$$
the self-adjoint sum of
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clause (c)
(well defined because $S_{i}$ is bounded and strongly commutes with $L_{i}$;
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-product-flow-generator]] clause (a),
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). The model reads
$(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable, the
$i$-th **total angular momentum**; its flow is the coordinate subgroup
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ of the lifted rotation action, using the physical-axes cover $\rho(W)=C^{-1}\rho_0(W)C$ defined in that lemma (rather than the literal quaternion-coordinate cover $\rho_0$),
$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}$
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clauses (b),(c)).

**(e) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(d) fix the angular momentum vocabulary
of this page within P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the cited readings. No new
physical assumption is added; in particular no magnetic coupling, no
spin-orbit interaction, no SU(2) gauge structure and no anomaly is
introduced. Whether a laboratory angular momentum measurement is described by
one of the assigned pairs $(L_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$, $(S_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ or
$(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ is a tested identification with
uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7, not a
consequence of this definition; no measurement procedure, apparatus,
resolution or empirical value is supplied here. Antiunitary symmetries,
superselection rules and symmetries of preparations as opposed to dynamics
are outside the definition.

post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-mome.physical_scope: The effective magnetic-moment coupling of the framework's massive spin-s particle model in a declared inertial frame, for a prescribed real bounded measurable magnetic field profile and a declared real gyromagnetic parameter gamma_s: the magnetic moment mu = gamma_s S with unit J T^-1, the Zeeman energy operator H_Z on the domain of the free operator, its units, and the status of gamma_s and of the field profile as empirical or externally prescribed model inputs. The item asserts no Maxwell equation, no source model, no derivation of gamma_s from charge and mass, no spin-orbit or relativistic correction, no dynamics and no measured value; it is a model assumption adopted on this page only.

post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-mome:
## Postulate

Adopt as a physical assumption of the framework, for the declared massive
spin-$s$ particle model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] and only within the
scope stated below, the following **effective magnetic-moment coupling**
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]).

**(i) Gyromagnetic parameter and magnetic moment.** For the declared spin
label $s$ assign a real **gyromagnetic parameter** $\gamma_{s}$, with unit
$\mathrm{s^{-1}\,T^{-1}}$, and define the **magnetic moment** of the model as
the internal-factor operator
$$\boldsymbol\mu:=\gamma_{s}\mathbf S=(\gamma_{s}S_{1},\gamma_{s}S_{2},\gamma_{s}S_{3}),$$
with unit $\mathrm{J\,T^{-1}}$. Here $\mathbf S=(S_{1},S_{2},S_{3})$ are the
spin operators of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] read on
the internal factor as in
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (c). The
parameter $\gamma_{s}$ is an empirical model parameter of the species: it is
part of the declared model data, with uncertainty, and it is not derived from
$s$, from the mass parameter $m$ or from the charge of the particle; no
relation between $\gamma_{s}$ and any other species parameter is asserted by
this postulate.

**(ii) Prescribed field and Zeeman energy operator.** Let
$\mathbf B:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R^{3}$ be a real bounded measurable
vector field, the **prescribed magnetic field profile**, with components
$B_{i}$ in tesla, entering the model as externally prescribed data
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]); in the
declared inertial frame the model adopts the **Zeeman energy operator**
$$H_{Z}:=H_{0}+M_{W},\qquad H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad M_{W}f:=-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\gamma_{s}B_{i}(\cdot)\bigl(S_{i}f\bigr)(\cdot),$$
on the componentwise domain
$D(H_{Z}):=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, the domain of $H_{0}$
(componentwise, [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]];
$\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ is the componentwise free operator with that domain by
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) applied to each component). The added term $M_{W}$ is bounded with
$\|M_{W}\|\le|\gamma_{s}|\sum_{i}\|B_{i}\|_{\infty}\max_{i}\|S_{i}\|$, so
$H_{Z}$ is a bounded self-adjoint perturbation of $H_{0}$ on the unchanged
domain, with unit joule, and the assignment $t\mapsto e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}$ is
a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group read in the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). The profile
$\mathbf B$ is a model input; the items of this page assert neither the
Maxwell equations nor a source or boundary realization of $\mathbf B$, and
the boundedness of $\mathbf B$ is an explicit hypothesis, not a general
property of magnetic fields.

**(iii) What is assumed and what is not.** (a) The coupling
$-\boldsymbol\mu\cdot\mathbf B(Q)$ is an **effective interaction**: it is
adopted, not derived from the spin representation P6, from the
minimal-coupling postulate P5a of the framework or from classical
electromagnetism. (b) No value of $\gamma_{s}$ and no comparison with
measured gyromagnetic ratios or $g$-factors is made here. (c) No spin-orbit
coupling, no fine or hyperfine structure, no relativistic correction and no
radiation reaction is included. (d) A time-dependent field profile requires
its own domain and evolution hypotheses and is outside this postulate. (e)
The internal factor is not a spatial current distribution and $\boldsymbol\mu$
is not asserted to arise from a rotating charge distribution.

(iv) **Status.** This postulate is an adopted model assumption with the
physical scope above; it is motivated by and formulated after the cited
sources, which treat the coupling as a model input, and no deduction of it
from the framework's other postulates is claimed.

pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the state, observable and kinematics postulates P1, P2, P5 and of the internal spin assignment P6 for the massive spin-s model: the spectra and Born outcome laws of the directional spin components n·S, the Casimir operator S^2 = hbar^2 s(s+1) I and, for s = 1/2, the explicit spin-up/spin-down probabilities. The item concerns the internal factor only; it asserts no dynamics, no magnetic coupling, no apparatus model, no measured spin value and no empirical identification of the operators.

pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor assignment of the spin postulate P6, read for the massive
spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with
mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and
$r=2s+1$, together with the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]), and assume
the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, let $\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ be the
outcome law of an assigned sharp observable $A$ in the pure preparation of a
unit vector $\psi$, and for a unit vector $n=(n_{1},n_{2},n_{3})\in\mathbb
R^{3}$ put $S_{n}:=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$, the matrix action of the self-adjoint
matrix $\hbar\,n\cdot J$ on the internal factor. Then:

(a) for every unit $n$ the operator $S_{n}$ is a bounded self-adjoint
operator on $H_{s}$ with spectrum
$\sigma(S_{n})=\hbar\{-s,-s+1,\dots,s\}$, and for each
$m\in\{-s,\dots,s\}$ the eigenspace $\ker(S_{n}-\hbar m)$ is the range of the
fibrewise orthogonal projection $P_{n,m}$ onto the eigenline of the matrix
$n\cdot J$ with eigenvalue $m$; consequently, for every unit $\psi\in H_{s}$,
$$\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar m\})=\|P_{n,m}\psi\|^{2}=\langle P_{n,m}\psi,\psi\rangle\qquad(m=-s,\dots,s),$$
and the law is concentrated on the finite set $\hbar\{-s,\dots,s\}$;

(b) the Casimir operator $S^{2}=S_{x}^{2}+S_{y}^{2}+S_{z}^{2}$ equals
$\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$ as a bounded operator, so for every preparation $\rho$ the
law of $S^{2}$ is the Dirac law at $\hbar^{2}s(s+1)$, and one has the
commutation relations
$[S_{i},S_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}S_{k}$ and
$[S^{2},S_{i}]=0$ on $H_{s}$, componentwise on the internal factor;

(c) for $s=\tfrac12$, every unit $n$ and every unit $\psi\in H_{1/2}$ one has
$$P_{n,\pm}=\tfrac12\bigl(I\pm n\cdot\sigma\bigr),\qquad \mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}\Bigl(\Bigl\{\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\Bigr\}\Bigr) =\frac{1}{2}\Bigl(1\pm\langle(n\cdot\sigma)\psi,\psi\rangle\Bigr),$$
where $n\cdot\sigma$ is applied fibrewise; in particular,
$\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar/2\})+\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{-\hbar/2\})=1$ and
each number lies in $[0,1]$;

(d) **Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5 and
P6 and the cited finite-dimensional mathematics; they concern the internal
factor of the model. They assert no dynamics, no magnetic coupling, no
measurement or apparatus model, no joint measurement of two spin components,
no value of $\hbar$ and no empirical spin value. In particular the statements
do not identify the operators $S_{n}$ with any laboratory spin measurement,
and they contain no comparison with data.

pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-eigen.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of P1, P2, P5 and P6 for the massive spin-s model and its orbital generators: for a smooth compactly supported radial profile times a spherical harmonic, the model vector is an eigenvector of the third orbital generator with eigenvalue hbar m, the Casimir quadratic form takes the value hbar^2 l(l+1), and the orbital quantum numbers are those of the spherical harmonic family. The statement concerns the spatial factor only, uses no dynamics and no measurement model, and asserts no spectral decomposition of the full spatial Hilbert space, no hydrogen spectrum and no empirical result.

pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-eigen:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor assignment of the spin postulate P6, read for the massive
spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] and
the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom
of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $l\ge0$, $m\in\{-l,\dots,l\}$, a unit vector
$w\in\mathbb C^{r}$ and a complex-valued $R\in C_{c}^{\infty}((0,\infty))$, and
let $h_{lm}$ be the harmonic homogeneous polynomial of degree $l$ with
$h_{lm}|_{S^2}=Y_{lm}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-harmonic-polynomial-dimension]] clause (c)
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]]). Define
the model vector
$$\psi(x):=R(|x|)\,h_{lm}(x)\,w\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^{3},\ x\ne0),\qquad \psi(0):=0 .$$
Then:

(a) $\psi$ is a well-defined class in the model's state space $H_{s}$ and in
fact $\psi\in C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})\subseteq\mathcal
S^{(r)}$; it lies in $D(L_{i})$ for each $i$, and for $x\ne0$
$$(L_{i}\psi)(x)=R(|x|)\,\bigl(-i\hbar\,D_{i}h_{lm}\bigr)(x)\,w,\qquad D_{i}h_{lm}=(x\times\nabla h_{lm})_{i},$$
so that $-i\hbar D_{i}h_{lm}$ is the polynomial representative of the sphere
function $L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]]; in particular
$L_{3}\psi=\hbar m\,\psi$;

(b) with $\|R\|_{l}^{2}:=\int_{0}^{\infty}|R(r)|^{2}r^{2l+2}\,dr$ one has
$\|\psi\|^{2}=\|R\|_{l}^{2}$ and
$$\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}=\|R\|_{l}^{2}\,\bigl\|L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}\bigr\|^{2}, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^{3}\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)\,\|\psi\|^{2},$$
so the Casimir quadratic form of the model's orbital generators on $\psi$
takes the value $\hbar^{2}l(l+1)$;

(c) consequently, for the pure preparation of the unit vector
$\psi/\|\psi\|$ (for $R\not\equiv0$), the mean and the second moment of the
outcome law of $(L_{3},\mathrm{J\,s})$ are finite and equal
$\hbar m$ and $\hbar^{2}m^{2}$, so the variance vanishes; for each $i$ the
mean and second moment of the law of $L_{i}$ are finite and the second moment
equals $\bigl\|L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}\bigr\|^{2}$; the model reads $(l,m)$
as the **orbital angular momentum quantum numbers** of the preparation, in
the sense of the eigenvalue of the angular momentum-squared form and the
eigenvalue of $L_{3}$;

(d) **Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5, P6
and the cited mathematics, and concern the spatial factor of the massive
model. The item asserts no dynamics, no measurement or apparatus model, no
joint sharp values of two different components $L_{i},L_{j}$, no empirical
value and no spectral resolution of $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$: the identity
$\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)$ is a quadratic-form statement on the
displayed smooth vectors and is not read as a statement about a self-adjoint
operator $\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}$ on the full spatial Hilbert space.

pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-total-conserv.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 for the declared isolated massive spin-s model with a real bounded measurable spin-independent potential invariant under every spatial rotation: the lifted coordinate rotation subgroups are one-parameter symmetry groups, and each total angular momentum component is a conserved assigned sharp observable whose outcome law is time-independent in every preparation, with conserved mean and second moment on D(L_i). The item asserts no symmetry of any concrete system, no spin-dependent or singular potential, no measurement procedure and no empirical result.

pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-total-conserv:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6, read for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$ and spin label $s$, together with the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]], and
assume the Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Dependent Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) and the readings of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Let $V:\mathbb
R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and measurable with
$V\circ R^{-1}=V$ almost everywhere for every $R\in SO(3)$, let
$$H_{V}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
be the model's spin-independent bounded-potential energy operator on
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with flow
$U(t)=e^{-itH_{V}/\hbar}$ in the reading of P4, and let
$J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}=L_{i}+S_{i}$ be the total angular momenta of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clause
(d). Then:

(a) for each $i$ the lifted coordinate rotation family
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clause (c) is a
strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group of symmetries of the declared
dynamics: $U_{s}(A_{i}(t))\,U(u)=U(u)\,U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ for all $t,u$ and
$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))D(H_{V})=D(H_{V})$;

(b) each $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is a conserved assigned sharp observable of
the model with energy $H_{V}$: for every preparation $\rho$, every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
and for a unit vector $\psi\in D(L_{i})=D(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}})$ the mean and
the second moment of the law of $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ in the pure
preparation $[\psi(t)]$ are finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero
values $\langle J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and
$\|J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}\psi\|^{2}$;

(c) in the same situation each spin component $S_{i}$ and each orbital
generator $L_{i}$ is a conserved assigned sharp observable in the same sense,
the laws of $S_{i}$ and $L_{i}$ being time-independent in every preparation;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and the
cited results, and concerns the declared isolated model with a real bounded
measurable potential invariant under every spatial rotation. It asserts no
symmetry of any concrete external field or apparatus, excludes spin-dependent,
singular and unbounded potentials (which require their own domain and symmetry
arguments), introduces no measurement, detector or empirical record, and
makes no claim that a definite numerical value of $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is
revealed at each time: the conserved object is the outcome law.

The lifted rotations use the physical-axes cover $\rho(W)=C^{-1}\rho_0(W)C$ fixed in [[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]]; its coordinate subgroups satisfy $\rho(A_i(t))=R_i(t)$, so the total generators retain the stated signs and axes.

pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-zeeman-preces.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and of the adopted effective magnetic-moment coupling, for a uniform static magnetic field along the third axis of a declared inertial frame: self-adjointness and factorization of the Zeeman energy operator, conservation of the spin component along the field, and Larmor precession of the transverse spin expectations with angular frequency gamma_s B_z. The item concerns the declared model only; it excludes inhomogeneous and time-dependent fields, radiation and relaxation, asserts no measured precession frequency or gyromagnetic ratio, and identifies no apparatus.

pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-zeeman-preces:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6, read for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$ and spin label $s$, together with the effective magnetic-moment coupling
adopted in [[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] and the
angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]], and
assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix a real constant
$B_{z}\in\mathbb R$ and use the uniform static field profile
$\mathbf B(x):=(0,0,B_{z})$, so that the Zeeman energy operator of the
postulate is
$$H_{Z}=H_{0}-\gamma_{s}B_{z}S_{3},\qquad H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad D(H_{Z})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
with flow $U_{Z}(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}$, and put $\omega:=\gamma_{s}B_{z}$
with unit $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. For a unit vector $\psi\in H_{s}$ put
$\psi(t):=U_{Z}(t)\psi$ and $\langle S_{i}\rangle(t):=\langle
S_{i}\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$. Then:

(a) $H_{Z}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{Z})$ and
$$U_{Z}(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\,e^{it\gamma_{s}B_{z}S_{3}/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
so in particular the transverse means satisfy, for every $t$,
$$\langle S_{1}\rangle(t)=\cos(\omega t)\langle S_{1}\rangle(0)+\sin(\omega t)\langle S_{2}\rangle(0),\qquad \langle S_{2}\rangle(t)=\cos(\omega t)\langle S_{2}\rangle(0)-\sin(\omega t)\langle S_{1}\rangle(0),$$
and the transverse vector $\bigl(\langle S_{1}\rangle(t),\langle S_{2}\rangle(t)\bigr)$
is the rotation of $\bigl(\langle S_{1}\rangle(0),\langle S_{2}\rangle(0)\bigr)$
by the angle $-\omega t$ in the $(1,2)$-plane;

(b) the component along the field is conserved: $S_{3}U_{Z}(t)=U_{Z}(t)S_{3}$
and $\langle S_{3}\rangle(t)=\langle S_{3}\rangle(0)$ for every unit $\psi$
and every $t$; more generally the outcome law of $S_{3}$ is time-independent
in every preparation;

(c) the conjugation identities
$$e^{itH_{Z}/\hbar}S_{1}e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}=\cos(\omega t)S_{1}+\sin(\omega t)S_{2},\qquad e^{itH_{Z}/\hbar}S_{2}e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}=\cos(\omega t)S_{2}-\sin(\omega t)S_{1}$$
hold as bounded operator identities, and with $S^{2}=\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$
(the Casimir operator of the model) also $S^{2}U_{Z}(t)=U_{Z}(t)S^{2}$;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and the
adopted coupling; it concerns the uniform static field $\mathbf B=(0,0,B_{z})$
with $B_{z}\in\mathbb R$ and the declared isolated model. It excludes
inhomogeneous and time-dependent fields, spin-dependent spatial potentials,
radiation, relaxation and environment coupling, asserts no measured
precession frequency and no measured gyromagnetic parameter, and identifies
no apparatus: $\omega=\gamma_{s}B_{z}$ is a model quantity computed from
assigned model parameters.

pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-stern-gerlach.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and of the adopted effective magnetic-moment coupling for the spin-half model in a static field profile B = (0,0,B_z(x_1)) whose component B_z is C^1 with bounded value and derivative: the identification of the model's Zeeman operator with the smooth bounded-coefficient force model, conservation of the field-aligned spin component and of the sector weights, the conditional rate gamma_s hbar G/2 of the transverse mean momentum in the spin-up sector when the gradient equals G on the support of the transverse marginal, and the divergence-free, curl identity of the profile. The item asserts no apparatus, no measured trajectory, no beam splitting observation and no source-free field realization; it is a model prediction conditional on its stated preparation assumptions.

pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-stern-gerlach:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6, read for the massive spin-$\tfrac12$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$ and spin label $s=\tfrac12$, together with the effective
magnetic-moment coupling of
[[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] with parameter
$\gamma_{1/2}\in\mathbb R$ and the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom
of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $B_{z}\in C^{1}(\mathbb R)$ be real with
$B_{z}$ and $B_{z}'$ bounded, let
$$\mathbf B(x):=\bigl(0,0,B_{z}(x_{1})\bigr),$$
let $H_{Z}$ be the Zeeman operator of the magnetic-moment postulate for this
profile, acting on $H_{1/2}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2})$ with domain
$D(H_{Z})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2})$, and let $u(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}u_{0}$
be its flow. Identify $H_{1/2}$ with
$\mathcal H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\oplus L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
through the internal basis $(e_{1/2},e_{-1/2})$, and let $P_{+}:=\tfrac12(I+2S_{3}/\hbar)$
be the fibrewise orthogonal projection onto the spin-up line $e_{1/2}$.
Then:

(a) under this identification $H_{Z}$ is the operator
$$K(u_{+},u_{-})=\Bigl(\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{j}P_{j}^{2}u_{+}-\frac{\gamma_{1/2}\hbar}{2}B_{z}(Q_{x})u_{+},\ \frac{1}{2m}\sum_{j}P_{j}^{2}u_{-}+\frac{\gamma_{1/2}\hbar}{2}B_{z}(Q_{x})u_{-}\Bigr),\qquad D(K)=W^{2,2}\oplus W^{2,2},$$
of [[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-conditional-stern-gerlach-force]] with
$\gamma_{s}:=\gamma_{1/2}$; consequently $H_{Z}$ is self-adjoint,
$S_{3}H_{Z}=H_{Z}S_{3}$ on $D(H_{Z})$, the sector weights
$\|P_{\pm}u(t)\|^{2}$ and the mean $\langle S_{3}\rangle_{u(t)}$ are
independent of $t$;

(b) if in addition $u_{0}\in D(H_{Z}^{2})$ is a unit vector with
$P_{+}u_{0}=u_{0}$ and $B_{z}'(x_{1})=G$ for every $x_{1}$ in a Borel set
$N\subseteq\mathbb R$ satisfying
$\int_{\mathbb R\setminus N}\eta_{+}(x_{1})\,dx_{1}=0$, where
$\eta_{+}(x_{1}):=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|u_{0}^{+}(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})|^{2}\,dx_{2}\,dx_{3}$
is the first-coordinate marginal density of the spin-up component, then
$$\frac{d}{dt}\Bigr|_{t=0}\bigl\langle P_{x}u(t),u(t)\bigr\rangle=\frac{\gamma_{1/2}\hbar}{2}\,G ;$$
for $t\ne0$ the general rate is
$\frac{d}{dt}\langle P_{x}u(t),u(t)\rangle=\gamma_{1/2}\langle S_{3}B_{z}'(Q_{x})u(t),u(t)\rangle$;

(c) the profile satisfies $\operatorname{div}\mathbf B=0$ and
$\operatorname{curl}\mathbf B=(0,-B_{z}'(x_{1}),0)$ at every point of
$\mathbb R^{3}$, as identities of the displayed components;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and the
adopted coupling. Clause (b) is a model prediction for the rate of the mean
transverse momentum of a prepared spin-up state under the marginal-support
hypothesis; it is not an observation of a beam splitting, a trajectory or a
count, it identifies no apparatus, calibration or detector, and it asserts
neither a source-free realization of $\mathbf B$ nor a Maxwell solution.
The word "Stern-Gerlach" names this conditional model, not a reported
experiment; no measured value of $\gamma_{1/2}$ enters and no empirical
conclusion is drawn.

pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-two-spin-comp.physical_scope: The internal-factor reading of the composition of two declared spin labels s and t under the composition postulate P1 and the spin assignment P6: the total spin operators on the tensor product of the two internal factors, their commutation relations and Casimir, the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition into total-spin blocks with multiplicities, and the explicit spin-half singlet. The item concerns the internal factors only; the full two-particle spatial model, statistics, interactions and any measured correlation belong to the composites pages and are not asserted here.

pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-two-spin-comp:
## Statement

Adopt the composition postulate P1 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6 in the readings of
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] and
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix two declared
spin labels $s,t\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ with internal factors
$V_{s}=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$, $V_{t}=\mathbb C^{2t+1}$ and spin matrices
$J^{(s)}_{i}$, $J^{(t)}_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]], and consider the
composite internal factor $V_{s}\otimes V_{t}$ with the tensor-product
representation $D_{s}\otimes D_{t}$ assigned by P6 clause (ii). Put
$$S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}:=\hbar\bigl(J^{(s)}_{i}\otimes I_{V_{t}}+I_{V_{s}}\otimes J^{(t)}_{i}\bigr),\qquad S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}:=\sum_{i=1}^{3}\bigl(S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}\bigr)^{2},\qquad S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{z}:=S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{3}.$$
Then:

(a) each $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}$ is a self-adjoint endomorphism of
$V_{s}\otimes V_{t}$ satisfying
$[S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i},S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{k}$,
$S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}$ is self-adjoint and commutes with every
$S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}$, and
$$S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}=S^{(s)2}\otimes I_{V_{t}}+I_{V_{s}}\otimes S^{(t)2}+2\sum_{i=1}^{3}S^{(s)}_{i}\otimes S^{(t)}_{i};$$

(b) there is an orthogonal decomposition
$V_{s}\otimes V_{t}=\bigoplus_{j=|s-t|}^{s+t}W_{j}$ into
$S^{\mathrm{tot}}$-invariant subspaces with $\dim W_{j}=2j+1$, on each of
which the triple $(S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{1},S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{2},S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{3})$
is unitarily equivalent to the spin-$j$ matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] scaled by $\hbar$; in
particular $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}=\hbar^{2}j(j+1)I$ on $W_{j}$, each $j$ occurs
exactly once, and there is an orthonormal basis $(v_{j,k})$,
$0\le k\le2j$, of $W_{j}$ with
$$S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{z}v_{j,k}=\hbar(j-k)v_{j,k},\qquad S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{+}v_{j,k}=\hbar\sqrt{k(2j-k+1)}\,v_{j,k-1},\qquad S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{-}v_{j,k}=\hbar\sqrt{(k+1)(2j-k)}\,v_{j,k+1};$$
the coefficients of the $v_{j,k}$ in the product basis $(e^{(s)}_{m}\otimes e^{(t)}_{n})$
are the Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and are determined by the phase of the
top vector $u_{j}$ (a unit vector of $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{z}$-weight $\hbar j$
orthogonal to all $W_{j'}$ with $j'>j$), with $u_{s+t}=e^{(s)}_{s}\otimes e^{(t)}_{t}$
admissible;

(c) for every $M$ the $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{z}$-eigenspace with weight $\hbar M$
has dimension $N(M)=\#\{m\in\{-s,\dots,s\}:M-m\in\{-t,\dots,t\}\}$, and the
identity $(e^{(s)}_{m}\otimes e^{(t)}_{n})_{m,n}$ is an orthonormal basis of
$V_{s}\otimes V_{t}$ of $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{z}$-eigenvectors with weights
$\hbar(m+n)$;

(d) for $s=t=\tfrac12$ one has $V_{1/2}\otimes V_{1/2}=W_{0}\oplus W_{1}$ with
$\dim W_{0}=1$ and $\dim W_{1}=3$; the vector
$$\Psi:=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(e^{(1/2)}_{1/2}\otimes e^{(1/2)}_{-1/2}-e^{(1/2)}_{-1/2}\otimes e^{(1/2)}_{1/2}\bigr)$$
is a unit vector with $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}\Psi=0$ for every $i$, and it is
the unique element of the kernel of $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}$ up to a phase;

(e) **Scope.** The statement concerns the internal factors of a declared
composite and the assignments of P1 and P6. It asserts no spatial
two-particle model, no statistics or permutation symmetry, no interaction, no
dynamics, no measurement and no empirical correlation; in particular it does
not by itself imply the singlet correlations of a separated pair, which
belong to the composites page.

rem-nrqm-angular-momentum-scope-and-empi.physical_scope: The scope and empirical status of the angular momentum and spin page: which postulates are adopted, which conditional results are proved, which empirical parameters remain input data with uncertainty, and which laboratory, relativistic and interaction structures are excluded. The remark asserts no model fact, no measurement and no empirical conclusion.

ex-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-half-direc.physical_scope: An exact computation inside the massive spin-half model of the framework: the Bloch parametrization of a unit internal spinor, the Born probabilities of the directional spin component n·S, and worked cases including the coordinate directions and the state e_{1/2}. The example uses the model's own outcome law; it involves no dynamics, no magnetic coupling, no apparatus model, no measurement record and no empirical value.

ex-nrqm-angular-momentum-l-eigenfunction.physical_scope: Explicit low-degree computations inside the angular theory of the massive model: the degree-zero and degree-one spherical harmonics, their orthonormality on the sphere and their eigenvalue equations for the third orbital generator and the orbital Casimir form, together with the citation of the general eigenstate theorem. The example concerns the spatial angular factor; it asserts no dynamics, no radial spectrum, no measurement and no empirical value.

ex-nrqm-angular-momentum-zeeman-toy-mode.physical_scope: A worked example inside the massive spin-half model with the adopted effective magnetic-moment coupling in a uniform static field: the exact sector identities for the Zeeman operator on product states, the energy offsets, and an explicitly labeled two-level truncation in which the internal levels differ by gamma hbar B_z and the spin precesses with angular frequency gamma B_z. The truncation is a toy model assumption, not derived from the full operator; no spectroscopy, no radiation, no measured gyromagnetic parameter and no apparatus is asserted.

texp-nrqm-angular-momentum-stern-gerlach.physical_scope: An idealized model prediction of the spin-half Zeeman model with a static windowed-gradient field: under an explicitly hypothetical containment premise (the first-coordinate marginals of both spin-sector components remain supported in the window of constant gradient during [0,tau]), the sector mean transverse momenta separate at the rate gamma hbar G / 2 and by gamma hbar G tau over the time tau, while the sector weights and the total transverse mean are conserved. The item is a hypothetical calculation, not a reported experiment: it asserts no apparatus, no beam, no counts, no detector, no measured value and no claim that the containment premise holds for realistic preparations.

texp-nrqm-angular-momentum-stern-gerlach:
## Statement

Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the effective magnetic-moment
coupling as in
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-stern-gerlach-conditional-force]], for the
massive spin-$\tfrac12$ model with mass parameter $m>0$ and parameter
$\gamma:=\gamma_{1/2}\in\mathbb R$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]]), and assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a real
$B_{z}\in C^{1}(\mathbb R)$ with $B_{z}$, $B_{z}'$ bounded, reals $0<a<\infty$
and $G$, and the field profile $\mathbf B(x)=(0,0,B_{z}(x_{1}))$, and
**suppose** that $B_{z}'(x_{1})=G$ for every $x_{1}\in(-a,a)$. Let
$H_{Z}$ be the Zeeman operator of the model with flow
$u(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}u_{0}$ for a unit vector
$u_{0}\in D(H_{Z}^{2})$, let
$u_{\pm}(t):=P_{\pm}u(t)$ be the two spin-sector components with
$P_{\pm}=\tfrac12(I\pm 2S_{3}/\hbar)$, and write
$w_{\pm}:=\|u_{\pm}(0)\|^{2}$ and, for each sign, let
$$\eta_{\pm}(t,x_{1}):=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}\bigl|u_{\pm}^{\pm}(t,x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})\bigr|^{2}\,dx_{2}\,dx_{3}$$
be the first-coordinate marginal density of the $\pm$ component of
$u_{\pm}(t)$, where $u_{\pm}^{\pm}$ denotes that nonzero component. Fix
$\tau>0$ and adopt the following **hypothetical containment premise**: for
each sign and every $t\in[0,\tau]$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R\setminus(-a,a)}\eta_{\pm}(t,x_{1})\,dx_{1}=0 .$$
Then:

(i) the sector weights are conserved: $\|u_{\pm}(t)\|^{2}=w_{\pm}$ for every
$t$, and $\langle S_{3}\rangle_{u(t)}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}(w_{+}-w_{-})$ is
independent of $t$;

(ii) under the containment premise, for each sign with $w_{\pm}>0$ the
normalized sector transverse mean
$M_{\pm}(t):=w_{\pm}^{-1}\langle P_{x}u_{\pm}(t),u_{\pm}(t)\rangle$ is affine
in $t$ on $[0,\tau]$:
$$\frac{d}{dt}M_{\pm}(t)=\pm\frac{\gamma\hbar G}{2},\qquad M_{\pm}(\tau)=M_{\pm}(0)\pm\frac{\gamma\hbar G\tau}{2},$$
so the two sector mean transverse momenta (both defined when $w_{+}w_{-}>0$)
differ by $\gamma\hbar G\tau$ at time $\tau$, independently of the initial
means; a sector with $w_{\pm}=0$ is trivial;

(iii) the total transverse mean evolves by the weighted rate
$$\frac{d}{dt}\bigl\langle P_{x}u(t),u(t)\bigr\rangle =\frac{\gamma\hbar G}{2}(w_{+}-w_{-})=\gamma G\,\langle S_{3}\rangle_{u_{0}}, \qquad t\in[0,\tau],$$
so for the equal-weight preparation $w_{+}=w_{-}=\tfrac12$ the total
transverse mean is conserved while the sector means separate;

(iv) **Status and scope.** This is an idealized hypothetical calculation: the
containment premise is an explicitly assumed possible property of the
evolved state, not an observed fact and not a consequence of the model; no
position-space splitting, detector trace, count, calibration or measured
value is asserted, no apparatus is modeled, and the historical
Stern-Gerlach experiment is not described or explained by this item. The
identification of the model with any real beam experiment remains a tested
identification with uncertainty under
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]].
